answer: Make each new agent earn its reputation the slow way: it must complete small paid jobs under a ferrous audit trail that records every outcome on chain, so a fresh identity cannot buy trust overnight. A sybil farm burns cash keeping hundreds of idle accounts warm, like tending an ember that never catches fire, while real agents build a whisper network of repeat clients who vouch for past work. Attackers can copy a profile, but they cannot copy that history cheaply.
